4. Mistakes
Strong | Eventual
Balances | Feeds
Inventory | Likes
Uniqueness checks | Counters
findings.fix: Rename the section 'When to use which'. Keep the callout as the single mistake: using eventual consistency for money, inventory or uniqueness.

findings.summary: Sloppy quorums and hinted handoff are named as the reason R+W>N fails, but neither is ever explained.
findings.evidence: R+W>N alone is not linearizable. It breaks with sloppy quorums, hinted handoff or clock-based last-write-wins conflict resolution.
findings.fix: Add one line on each. A sloppy quorum counts acks from stand-in nodes outside the key's N replicas, so the read and write sets may not overlap. Hinted handoff means a stand-in node holds the write and forwards it to the real replica later.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "minutes").

findings.summary: The cheat sheet says R+W>N gives strong reads, but page 3 says R+W>N alone is not linearizable, so a skimmer would misread the rule.
findings.evidence: Page 6: 'R+W>N gives strong reads' vs page 3: 'R+W>N alone is not linearizable'
findings.fix: Reword the cheat sheet line to 'R+W>N makes the read set overlap the latest write set, but it is not linearizable under sloppy quorums, hinted handoff or LWW'.
